questions.knowledge_point: Applying Row Operations To a Coefficients Matrix
questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ on $X?$
questions.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $-3$ times the first row to the second row. 

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-3)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 3+(-3)(1) & -1+(-3)(2) & 1+(-3)(1) \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & -7 & -2 \\ 2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $B?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $4$ times the first row to the second row.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4 & 12 & 3 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+4\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ -4+(4)(1) & 12+(4)(3) & 3+(4)(6) \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ -1+1 & 2+3 & 4+6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 6 \\ 0 & 24 & 27 \\ 0 & 5 & 10\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ on $A?$
questions.worked_solution:
The operation ${R}_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}{R}_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:=(-\frac{1}{3})\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 6 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot (-3) & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 9 & (-\frac{1}{3})\cdot 0\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $U,$ given by

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $U?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}$ means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{2}.$

- The operation ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}U & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}\cdot {R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0+0 & -1+1 & -3+0 & 4+3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}].

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}{R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation ${R}_{1}↔{R}_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{1}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-1)\cdot {R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Appropriate Row Operation To Transform One Matrix Into Another
questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $E$ into the matrix $F$, where

$$
E=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7 \\ -3 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,F=[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st row is the same in both matrices. The only rows that have changed are the $2$nd row and the $3$rd row.   

By considering the given row operations that change both the $2$nd and the $3$rd row, we notice that 

$$
\begin{aligned}E & =[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7 \\ -3 & 1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 3 \\ -3 & 1 & -3 \\ 8 & -3 & 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =F.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}.
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following elementary row operations transforms the matrix $K$ into the matrix $L$, where

$$
K=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}],\,L=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]?
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has changed is the $2$nd row. 

By considering the given row operations that modify the $2$nd row, we notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}K & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 10 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =L.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}.
$$

By considering the given row operations that modify the $1$st row, we notice that

$$

$$

$$
X=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 5 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}5 & -5 & -10 \\ 5 & 6 & 10 \\ 1 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]?

$$

$$

Therefore, the required row operation is

$$
{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+5{R}_{3}.

$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Which elementary row operation could transform the matrix $A$ into the matrix $B$, where 

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, notice that the $1$st and the $3$rd rows are the same in both matrices. The only row that has been changed is the $2$nd row. 

Now, applying the operation $R_2:=R_2+1 \cdot R_1,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & 1 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+1\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 4+1\cdot (-4) & 1+1\cdot (-2) & 2+1\cdot 4 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-4 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & 6 \\ 1 & 2 & 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the transformation could be done by the operation 

$$
R_2:=R_2+1\cdot R_1
$$

or simply

$$
R_2:=R_2+R_1.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Given that
$[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]$ which elementary row operation could make $a_{22}=0?$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
In the given matrix, we have $a_{22}=5$ and we want to perform an elementary row operation that makes $a_{22}=0.$

- We *cannot* make $a_{22}=0$ by switching two rows, because there are no rows with $0$ as the second entry.

- We *cannot* multiply the second row by $0,$ because we are only allowed to multiply rows by *nonzero* constants.

- However, we *can* add a multiple of another row to the $2$nd row to make $a_{22}=0.$

Looking at the first row, we see that $a_{12}=1.$ If we add $-5$ times this entry to $a_{22},$ we will get $a_{22}=0$ as desired. So, the elementary row operation that we need to use is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1.
$$

Applying this operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 5 & 6 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\,{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-5)\cdot {R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -1+(-5)\cdot 3 & 5+(-5)\cdot 1 & 6+(-5)\cdot (-2) \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & -2 \\ -16 & 0 & 16 \\ 0 & 2 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the desired elemetary row operation is

$$
R_2 := R_2 + (-5) \cdot R_1,
$$

or simply

$$
R_2 := R_2 -5 R_1.
$$
